check.intro: The config on disk (what a reload would apply), like opencap check. Estimates assume {rtt} ms per request (poller.yaml check.est_rtt_ms).
common.name: Name

config.intro: Edits are written to the config files (revision {rev}) after the loader and the drivers accept them. Reload applies them; only changed channels restart. Channels, devices and tags live in devices.json, which a KEPServerEX re-import replaces: keep fixes that must survive a re-import in the device's override.
config.no_channels_yet_add: No channels yet: add one or import a KEPServerEX project.
config.the_config_on_disk: The config on disk does not load:
dashboard.no_channel_is_polled: No channel is polled. Open the config.
device.not_connected_right_now: Not connected right now: identity is read only over the device's existing connection (opencap does not open a second one).
device.plan_text: {tags} enabled tags in {blocks} block(s), {requests} request(s) per full pass, about {ms} ms per pass, channel load {pct}% (estimates).
device.read_every_tag_of: Read every tag of this device now (read-only)
device.subtitle: {driver} · {host}:{port} · topic {topic} · SubDeviceId {sub}
device.the_device_does_not: The device does not report an identity.
device.this_device_is_not: This device is not polled by the running poller: its channel is disabled, not selected with --site, the change is not reloaded yet, or it does not exist.
edit.confirm_delete_device: Delete device {id} with its {n} tag(s), its publish map entry and its override?
edit.confirm_remove_map: Remove the publish map entry of {id}?
edit.no_entry_the_device: No entry: the device publishes without a SubDeviceId.
edit.override_json_fields_enabled: Override (JSON; fields: enabled, host, port, scan_ms, min_scan_ms, timeout_ms, retries, demote_after, demote_for_ms, params, publish, tags). Empty removes it.
error.conflict: Someone changed the configuration since you loaded it. Load the page again, then redo your change.
import.a_kepserverex_project_json: A KEPServerEX project.json export replaces devices.json (as opencap import-kep) and adds stub SubDeviceIds for new devices to devices_map.yaml; your overrides and existing map entries are kept. An opencap export (Config › Export) restores the files it contains. Every import is a dry run first: nothing is written until you apply it, and the config must not change in between.
import.confirm_apply: Write the imported config? The current files are kept as .bak.
import.stubs_many: devices_map.yaml: {n} stub entries for new devices.
import.stubs_one: devices_map.yaml: {n} stub entry for new devices.
import.writes: writes {files} (the old files are kept as .bak)
login.use_an_api_token: Use an API token from poller.yaml api.tokens (or api.token_env). Viewer tokens can look; admin tokens can also change the configuration. The token stays in this browser tab only.
pending.disk_invalid: The config on disk does not load: {error}. A reload would fail and keep the running config.
quick.choose_a_device_on: Choose a device on the left to watch its tags.
quick.live_values_over_api: Live values over /api/v1/ws: changes arrive as they are polled, at most four updates per device per second. Read-only: nothing here writes to a PLC.
quick.read_every_tag_of: Read every tag of this device now (POST read-once, read-only)
quick.shown_note: Showing {shown} of {n} tags: filter to see the others.
quick.this_device_has_no: This device has no enabled tags.
quick.title_polling: The live feed (/api/v1/ws) is not available from this server: values are read with GET …/values every 2 s.
saved.comments_lost: Comments could not be kept in {files} (old text in .bak).
shell.no_api_token_is: No API token is configured, so this UI is read-only and answers only on localhost. Set api.tokens in poller.yaml to edit the configuration.
shell.read_only_towards_plcs: read-only towards PLCs: this UI never writes a PLC value · Alpine.js licence
shell.readonly_config: Configuration editing is off: {reason}. See docs/deployment.md (the config directory must be writable by opencap).
